patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, rash, or recent illnesses.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with swelling in the right knee and a familial history of similar problems.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi doctor. My parents brought me in because my right knee has been swollen since after I played in the park, and there wasn’t any clear injury. We haven’t had any fever or recent illness, and my mom says an uncle in her family had a similar problem.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any involuntary movements recently—like twitching, jerking, shaking, or sudden uncontrollable movements of your face, arms, or legs? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—there haven’t been any twitching, jerking, or sudden uncontrollable movements. It’s mainly the swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **lump in your right breast that doesn’t hurt** and feels like it **moves a bit under the skin** when you touch it? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—there’s no lump in my breast that doesn’t hurt or moves under the skin; the only issue I’ve had is swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: When you press or gently tap around your belly button area, does it feel tender or painful? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—when you press around my belly button, it doesn’t feel tender or painful.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been vomiting recently (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t been vomiting recently. I’m mainly just dealing with the swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump or mass in your **right breast** (for example, a new or growing area you can feel)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any lump or mass in my right breast. The only thing bothering me is the swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that the lenses in **both** of your eyes look **cloudy or hazy**, like you’re seeing through a film? (Yes/No)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—my eyes don’t look cloudy or hazy, and I’m not seeing through a film. It’s just the swelling in my right knee that we’re concerned about.”

turns.doctor_question: In the past few months, have you lost weight without trying (for example, your clothes fit looser or the scale went down), even though you didn’t change your diet or exercise?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t lost weight without trying, and my clothes and appetite seem about the same. It’s really only the swelling in my right knee that’s been going on.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a **lump or mass in your right breast that doesn’t hurt** (painless), even if it’s small?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—there isn’t any lump or mass in my right breast, and it doesn’t hurt; I’ve only had swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been pregnant, or is there any chance you could be pregnant right now?
turns.patient_answer: “No doctor, I can’t be pregnant—I’m an 18-month-old boy, and there’s no chance of pregnancy.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a breast lump or swelling that seems to move or shift when you touch it, rather than staying fixed in one spot?
turns.patient_answer: “No doctor, I haven’t noticed any breast lump or swelling at all—so there’s nothing that would move when touched. I’m only having the swelling in my right knee.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself avoiding using your right knee because it hurts? (yes/no)
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I’m still using my right knee as usual; it’s mainly the swelling we noticed after playing, without any clear pain focus. My parents just said the knee looked bigger than before.”
